Command: Break the neck of an unredeemed firstborn donkey
Summary: The command: Break the neck of an unredeemed firstborn donkey (Exodus 13:13). An unclean animal could not be offered, so if its owner would not redeem it with a lamb, its neck was broken instead.
Commandment: Break the neck of an unredeemed firstborn donkey, as prescribed in Exodus 13:13.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Redemption of the firstborn remembered that God spared Israel's firstborn in Egypt. The New Testament speaks of Jesus as the firstborn and of believers as redeemed, but does not continue the redemption payment as a Christian rite (Colossians 1:15-18; 1 Peter 1:18-19).
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: because the LORD slew all the firstborn in Egypt and spared Israel's, therefore the firstborn are his (Exodus 13:14-15).
